vocab.definition: Thomson's model: a ball of positive charge with electrons in it.
a tiny dense positive nucleus surrounded by electrons.
experiment that proved most of the atom is empty space.
Bohr's shells where electrons orbit at set distances.

misconceptions.wrong: The atom was discovered in one experiment.
misconceptions.right: The model changed over time as new evidence appeared.

misconceptions.wrong: Electrons were known before the nucleus.
misconceptions.right: Correct — but the nucleus was found later by Rutherford.

misconceptions.wrong: Neutrons were in the first models.
misconceptions.right: Chadwick discovered the neutron about 20 years later.

questions.text: Describe the plum pudding model of the atom. [2 marks]
Most alpha particles passed straight through the gold foil. Explain what this showed. [2 marks]
A few alpha particles bounced straight back. Explain what this told scientists. [2 marks]
State how Bohr changed the nuclear model. [1 mark]
Complete the order using the word bank. [2 marks]

footer.tip: New experimental evidence forces models to be revised.
footer.thinkPrompt: Why was the alpha-scattering experiment such strong evidence for a nucleus?
